result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.select_nodes_by_degree()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Select nodes by degree criteria. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5925-L5989){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.select_nodes_by_degree( min_degree=None, max_degree=None, degree_type="total" ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Filters nodes based on their degree (number of connections). Useful for finding hubs (high degree) or peripheral nodes (low degree). Can filter by in-degree, out-degree, or total degree. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [min_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Minimum degree threshold (inclusive). `None` means no lower bound. [max_degree]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum degree threshold (inclusive). `None` means no upper bound. [degree_type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["total"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Type of degree to use: `"in"`, `"out"`, or `"total"`. For undirected graphs, only `"total"` is valid. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Select high-degree hub nodes: ::: {#098f336b .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_star_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=5) ) # Hub node has degree 10, all others have degree 1 hubs = graph.get_selected_node_ids() # Returns 1 (the center node) len(hubs) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 1 ``` ::: ::: Filter by degree range: ::: {#f9fc3e55 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_path_graph(10) .select_nodes_by_degree(min_degree=1, max_degree=2, degree_type="out") ) # Selects nodes with 1-2 outgoing edges ``` :::
